However, low-spin tetrahedral complexes are extremely rare because pairing almost never occurs preferentially over occupying the $t_2$ orbitals. Thus, tetrahedral complexes are high-spin. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). In tetrahedral geometry, fewer ligands surround the metal ($4$ instead of $6$) and no ligand lies along the direct orientation of the $d$-orbitals, resulting in $\Delta_t = \frac{4}{9}\Delta_o$. Because $\Delta_t$ is inherently smaller than the electron pairing energy $P$ (i.e., $\Delta_t < P$), the energy required to pair electrons is greater than the energy required to promote them into the $t_2$ set. Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For an octahedral coordination entity containing a transition metal ion with a $d^4$ valence electron configuration, what are the ground state electronic configurations in a weak crystal field ($\Delta_o < P$) and in a strong crystal field ($\Delta_o > P$), respectively?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand electron distribution in an octahedral field for $d^4$. The first three electrons enter the degenerate $t_{2g}$ orbitals singly with parallel spins ($t_{2g}^3$), according to Hund's rule.
Step 2: Case 1: Weak field ($\Delta_o < P$). The pairing energy $P$ is greater than the crystal field splitting $\Delta_o$. Consequently, it is energetically more favorable for the fourth electron to enter the higher-energy $e_g$ orbital rather than pair up in a $t_{2g}$ orbital. This gives a high-spin configuration: $t_{2g}^3 e_g^1$.
Step 3: Case 2: Strong field ($\Delta_o > P$). The crystal field splitting $\Delta_o$ is greater than the pairing energy $P$. It is energetically cheaper to pair the fourth electron in a lower $t_{2g}$ orbital than promote it across the large gap $\Delta_o$. This gives a low-spin configuration: $t_{2g}^4 e_g^0$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding the practical and analytical applications of coordination compounds:

List I (Chelate / Coordination Complex)
A. $\text{Ca-EDTA}^{2-}$
B. Cisplatin
C. $[\text{Ni}(\text{dmg})_2]$
D. $[\text{RhCl}(\text{PPh}_3)_3]$

List II (Application / Use)
I. Gravimetric and qualitative detection of $\text{Ni}^{2+}$
II. Clinical antidote for lead ($\text{Pb}$) poisoning
III. Homogeneous hydrogenation catalyst for alkenes
IV. Chemotherapeutic agent for inhibiting tumor cell division

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
B) A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
C) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
D) A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match $\text{Ca-EDTA}^{2-}$ (A). Calcium disodium EDTA is administered in lead poisoning; lead replaces calcium due to the significantly higher thermodynamic stability constant of the $\text{Pb-EDTA}^{2-}$ chelate, which is excreted harmlessly in urine: A matches II.
Step 2: Match Cisplatin (B). $cis\text{-}[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$ is an anticancer drug that binds to cancer cell DNA, blocking replication: B matches IV.
Step 3: Match $[\text{Ni}(\text{dmg})_2]$ (C). Bis(dimethylglyoximato)nickel(II) forms as a red precipitate used for the selective detection and gravimetric determination of nickel: C matches I.
Step 4: Match $[\text{RhCl}(\text{PPh}_3)_3]$ (D). Wilkinson's catalyst is widely used for the homogeneous catalytic hydrogenation of alkenes: D matches III. Thus, the match is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding linkage isomerism:
(i) Linkage isomerism arises in a coordination compound containing an ambidentate ligand.
(ii) In the yellow complex $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{NO}_2)]\text{Cl}_2$, the nitrite ligand coordinates through nitrogen, whereas in the red complex $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{ONO})]\text{Cl}_2$, it coordinates through oxygen.
(iii) The thiocyanate ion ($\text{SCN}^-$) can coordinate through sulfur (thiocyanato) or through nitrogen (isothiocyanato).
(iv) Ethane-1,2-diamine coordinates through two different donor atoms and hence shows linkage isomerism.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: A) (i), (ii), and (iv) only
B) (i), (ii), and (iii) only
C) (ii) and (iii) only
D) (i), (iii), and (iv) only
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate statement (i). Linkage isomerism arises when an ambidentate ligand can coordinate through either of two different donor atoms. Statement (i) is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate statement (ii). In the yellow nitro isomer $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{NO}_2)]\text{Cl}_2$, $\text{NO}_2^-$ is coordinated via nitrogen ($-\text{NO}_2$). In the red nitrito isomer $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{ONO})]\text{Cl}_2$, it coordinates via oxygen ($-\text{ONO}$). Statement (ii) is correct.
Step 3: Evaluate statement (iii). $\text{SCN}^-$ can coordinate via sulfur ($\text{M}-\text{SCN}$, thiocyanato) or via nitrogen ($\text{M}-\text{NCS}$, isothiocyanato). Statement (iii) is correct.
Step 4: Evaluate statement (iv). Ethane-1,2-diamine ($\text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{NH}_2$) coordinates symmetrically through both of its identical nitrogen donor atoms; it is a symmetrical bidentate chelating ligand, not an ambidentate ligand, and does not show linkage isomerism. Statement (iv) is incorrect. Hence, only (i), (ii), and (iii) are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding theories of bonding in coordination compounds:
Statement I: Valence Bond Theory (VBT) provides no explanation for the color and electronic absorption spectra exhibited by transition metal complexes.
Statement II: Crystal Field Theory (CFT) considers the metal-ligand bond to be completely electrostatic (ionic), treating ligands as point charges or point dipoles and completely disregarding covalent orbital overlap.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
B) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
D) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. Although VBT explains geometry and magnetic properties qualitatively, it fails to explain the electronic absorption spectra and the origin of characteristic colors of coordination complexes because it does not account for splitting of $d$-orbital energy levels. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. CFT is an electrostatic model that assumes the interactions between the metal ion and the ligands are purely electrostatic. Ligands are treated as point negative charges (anions) or point dipoles (neutral molecules). It neglects covalent interactions between metal $d$-orbitals and ligand orbitals, which is its primary theoretical limitation. Statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The hexaamminecobalt(III) ion $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ is an inner orbital diamagnetic complex, whereas the hexafluoridocobaltate(III) ion $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$ is an outer orbital paramagnetic complex.
Reason (R): For $\text{Co}^{3+}$, $\text{NH}_3$ produces a strong crystal field with $\Delta_o > P$ forcing electron pairing in $3d$ orbitals ($d^2sp^3$), whereas $\text{F}^-$ produces a weak crystal field with $\Delta_o < P$ leaving four unpaired electrons ($sp^3d^2$).
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) (A) is false but (R) is true
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
C) (A) is true but (R) is false
D) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Determine the configuration of $\text{Co}^{3+}$. Cobalt is element $27$; $\text{Co}^{3+} = [\text{Ar}]\,3d^6$.
Step 2: Analyze $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$. $\text{NH}_3$ is a strong field ligand for trivalent cobalt ($\Delta_o > P$). The six $3d$ electrons pair completely into three $3d$ orbitals ($t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$), leaving two empty inner $3d$ orbitals. These two $3d$, one $4s$, and three $4p$ orbitals hybridize to form $d^2sp^3$ hybrid orbitals. With zero unpaired electrons, the complex is diamagnetic. Assertion (A) for $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ is true.
Step 3: Analyze $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$. Fluoride ($\text{F}^-$) is a weak field ligand ($\Delta_o < P$). Hund's rule is followed, resulting in four unpaired electrons ($t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$). Because inner $3d$ orbitals are not empty, outer $4s, 4p, 4d$ orbitals are hybridized ($sp^3d^2$), forming an outer orbital paramagnetic complex. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 4: Relate (A) and (R). Reason (R) provides the precise crystal field energetic reason ($\Delta_o$ vs $P$) and orbital hybridization description. Thus, both are true and (R) correctly explains (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When $0.1\text{ mol}$ of a chromium(III) complex having the empirical formula $\text{CrCl}_3 \cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$ was treated with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, it lost $1.8\text{ g}$ of water. In a separate experiment, treatment of $0.1\text{ mol}$ of the same complex with excess $\text{AgNO}_3(aq)$ yielded $0.2\text{ mol}$ of white precipitate of $\text{AgCl}$. What is the structural formula of this coordination compound?
options: A) $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2 \cdot \text{H}_2\text{O}$
B) $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4\text{Cl}_2]\text{Cl} \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$
C) $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]\text{Cl}_3$
D) $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_3\text{Cl}_3] \cdot 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the dehydration by concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$. Concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ removes only lattice water (water of crystallization outside the coordination sphere), leaving coordinated aqua ligands untouched. Moles of water lost per mole of complex:
$\text{Moles of } \text{H}_2\text{O} = \frac{1.8\text{ g}}{18\text{ g/mol}} = 0.1\text{ mol}$.
Since $0.1\text{ mol}$ of complex loses $0.1\text{ mol}$ of water, each formula unit contains exactly one water molecule outside the coordination sphere ($\cdot \text{H}_2\text{O}$).
Step 2: Analyze the silver chloride precipitation. Moles of $\text{AgCl}$ precipitated by $0.1\text{ mol}$ of complex = $0.2\text{ mol}$. Therefore, there are $2$ ionisable chloride ions outside the coordination sphere ($\text{Cl}_2$).
Step 3: Deduce the coordination sphere. With six total water molecules and three total chlorides: five water molecules and one chloride ion are coordinated to $\text{Cr}$ inside the bracket: $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2 \cdot \text{H}_2\text{O}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the octahedral coordination complex $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2(\text{py})_2\text{Cl}_2]^{2+}$, which conforms to the general formula $[\text{Ma}_2\text{b}_2\text{c}_2]$. What is the total number of stereoisomers (including geometrical and optical isomers) and how many pairs of enantiomers exist for this complex?
options: A) Total stereoisomers = $5$, Pairs of enantiomers = $0$
B) Total stereoisomers = $6$, Pairs of enantiomers = $1$
C) Total stereoisomers = $8$, Pairs of enantiomers = $2$
D) Total stereoisomers = $6$, Pairs of enantiomers = $2$
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Determine the number of geometrical isomers for an octahedral complex of type $[\text{Ma}_2\text{b}_2\text{c}_2]$. The spatial distribution of the pairs of identical ligands (trans vs cis relative to each other) gives five distinct geometrical isomers:
1. trans-a, trans-b, trans-c (all three pairs trans)
2. trans-a, cis-b, cis-c
3. cis-a, trans-b, cis-c
4. cis-a, cis-b, trans-c
5. cis-a, cis-b, cis-c (all three pairs cis)
Step 2: Check each geometrical isomer for chirality (symmetry elements). Isomer 1 has an inversion center ($i$) and planes of symmetry ($\sigma$), so it is achiral. Isomers 2, 3, and 4 each possess at least one plane of symmetry ($\sigma$), rendering them achiral as well.
Step 3: Analyze isomer 5 (all-cis). In the all-cis arrangement, where the two ligands of each pair are mutually cis ($90^\circ$), there is no plane of symmetry, center of inversion, or improper rotation axis ($S_n$). It belongs to the chiral point group $C_2$ and is asymmetric. Consequently, it exists as a pair of non-superimposable mirror images (one pair of enantiomers: $d$ and $l$ forms).
Step 4: Sum up the total stereoisomers. There are $4$ achiral geometrical isomers plus $2$ enantiomeric forms of the chiral all-cis isomer, giving a total of $4 + 2 = 6$ stereoisomers and exactly $1$ pair of enantiomers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding the infrared carbon-oxygen stretching frequency ($
u_{	ext{CO}}$) and synergic bonding in metal carbonyl complexes:
(I) Free gaseous carbon monoxide has a characteristic $	ext{C-O}$ stretching absorption band at approximately $2143	ext{ cm}^{-1}$.
(II) In neutral transition metal carbonyls such as $[	ext{Ni}(	ext{CO})_4]$, $
u_{	ext{CO}}$ is shifted to a lower frequency compared to free $	ext{CO}$ due to $d\pi ightarrow \pi^*$ backbonding.
(III) Across the isoelectronic series $[	ext{Mn}(	ext{CO})_6]^+$, $[	ext{Cr}(	ext{CO})_6]$, and $[	ext{V}(	ext{CO})_6]^-$, the $	ext{C-O}$ stretching frequency follows the order: $
u_{	ext{CO}}([	ext{V}(	ext{CO})_6]^-) < 
u_{	ext{CO}}([	ext{Cr}(	ext{CO})_6]) < 
u_{	ext{CO}}([	ext{Mn}(	ext{CO})_6]^+)$.
(IV) Replacing a $	ext{CO}$ ligand with a strong $\sigma$-donor ligand like $	ext{PMe}_3$ increases electron density on the metal, thereby decreasing $
u_{	ext{CO}}$ for the remaining carbonyl ligands.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: A) (I), (II), and (III) only
B) (II) and (IV) only
C) (I), (II), (III), and (IV)
D) (I), (III), and (IV) only
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate statement (I). Gaseous uncoordinated $\text{CO}$ possesses a strong fundamental infrared absorption band at $2143\text{ cm}^{-1}$, corresponding to its formal triple bond. Statement (I) is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate statement (II). Backdonation of electron density from the metal $d$-orbitals into the antibonding $\pi^*$ orbitals of $\text{CO}$ reduces the $\text{C-O}$ bond order (below 3), which reduces the force constant and decreases the stretching frequency $\nu_{\text{CO}}$ (typically $2000-2060\text{ cm}^{-1}$ in $[\text{Ni}(\text{CO})_4]$). Statement (II) is correct.
Step 3: Evaluate statement (III). In isoelectronic hexacarbonyls, negative charge on the metal increases from $\text{Mn}(+1)$ to $\text{Cr}(0)$ to $\text{V}(-1)$. More negative charge promotes greater $\pi$-backdonation into the $\pi^*$ orbital of $\text{CO}$, causing greater weakening of the $\text{C-O}$ bond and the lowest stretching frequency in $[\text{V}(\text{CO})_6]^-$ ($~1860\text{ cm}^{-1}$ vs $2000\text{ cm}^{-1}$ in $\text{Cr}(\text{CO})_6$ and $2090\text{ cm}^{-1}$ in $\text{Mn}(\text{CO})_6^+$). Statement (III) is correct.
Step 4: Evaluate statement (IV). A strong $\sigma$-donor (like $\text{PMe}_3$) donates electron density into the metal center without significant competing $\pi$-backacceptance. The excess electron density is transferred via enhanced $\pi$-backdonation into the remaining $\text{CO}$ ligands, weakening their bonds and decreasing $\nu_{\text{CO}}$. Statement (IV) is correct. Thus, all four statements (I, II, III, and IV) are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding Crystal Field Stabilization Energy ($\text{CFSE}$) calculations in octahedral geometry:
Statement I: The crystal field stabilization energy for a high-spin $d^5$ transition metal complex with configuration $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$ is exactly $0.0\Delta_o$.
Statement II: The net crystal field stabilization energy for a low-spin $d^7$ octahedral complex with configuration $t_{2g}^6 e_g^1$ relative to the free spherical ion is $-1.8\Delta_o + P$, where $P$ represents the pairing energy penalty.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
B) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
D) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. For high-spin $d^5$, the electronic configuration is $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$. The CFSE is calculated as:
$\text{CFSE} = [3 \times (-0.4\Delta_o)] + [2 \times (+0.6\Delta_o)] = -1.2\Delta_o + 1.2\Delta_o = 0.0\Delta_o$. There are no forced pairs relative to the free ion (zero pairing penalty). Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. For low-spin $d^7$, the configuration is $t_{2g}^6 e_g^1$. The orbital stabilization energy is:
$\text{Orbital CFSE} = [6 \times (-0.4\Delta_o)] + [1 \times (+0.6\Delta_o)] = -2.4\Delta_o + 0.6\Delta_o = -1.8\Delta_o$.
Now evaluate the pairing energy term: In the free $d^7$ ion (or high-spin $t_{2g}^5 e_g^2$), there are two electron pairs ($(\uparrow\downarrow)(\uparrow\downarrow)(\uparrow)(\uparrow)(\uparrow)$). In the low-spin $t_{2g}^6 e_g^1$ complex, there are three electron pairs. The number of additional forced pairs is $3 - 2 = 1$. Hence, the pairing energy term is $+1P$. The net $\text{CFSE} = -1.8\Delta_o + P$. Statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The trioxalatochromate(III) ion $[\text{Cr}(\text{ox})_3]^{3-}$ is paramagnetic with three unpaired electrons, whereas the trioxalatocobaltate(III) ion $[\text{Co}(\text{ox})_3]^{3-}$ is completely diamagnetic.
Reason (R): Oxalate is an oxygen-donor ligand that behaves as a weak field ligand for $\text{Cr}^{3+}$, but for $\text{Co}^{3+}$ having higher effective nuclear charge and smaller radius, the crystal field splitting exceeds the pairing energy ($\Delta_o > P$), resulting in a low-spin $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$ configuration.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
C) (A) is true but (R) is false
D) (A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). For $[\text{Cr}(\text{ox})_3]^{3-}$, $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ has a $3d^3$ configuration. In an octahedral field, three electrons occupy the three degenerate $t_{2g}$ orbitals singly ($t_{2g}^3 e_g^0$), yielding $3$ unpaired electrons ($n=3$, paramagnetic). For $[\text{Co}(\text{ox})_3]^{3-}$, experimental magnetic measurements show that it is diamagnetic with zero unpaired electrons ($n=0$). Thus, Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). Although oxalate ($\text{ox}^{2-}$) is positioned on the weak-field side of the spectrochemical series for divalent metals, $\text{Co}^{3+}$ has an exceptionally high effective nuclear charge and compact radius. This dramatically increases $\Delta_o$ such that $\Delta_o > P$ even with oxygen donors like oxalate and water. As a consequence, all six $3d$ electrons of $\text{Co}^{3+}$ pair up in the $t_{2g}$ orbitals, yielding a diamagnetic $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$ low-spin state. Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I (Coordination Complex) with List II (Stoichiometric precipitation behavior with excess $\text{AgNO}_3$ and electrical conductivity type):

List I
A. $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_3$
B. $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2$
C. $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]\text{Cl}$
D. $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_3\text{Cl}_3]$

List II
I. $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{AgCl}$ precipitated; $1:1$ electrolyte ($2$ ions per formula unit)
II. $0\text{ mol}$ of $\text{AgCl}$ precipitated; non-electrolyte (does not ionise)
III. $3\text{ mol}$ of $\text{AgCl}$ precipitated; $1:3$ electrolyte ($4$ ions per formula unit)
IV. $2\text{ mol}$ of $\text{AgCl}$ precipitated; $1:2$ electrolyte ($3$ ions per formula unit)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
B) A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
C) A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
D) A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_3$ (A). It dissociates into $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+} + 3\text{Cl}^-$. This produces $4$ ions ($1:3$ electrolyte) and precipitates $3\text{ mol}$ of $\text{AgCl}$: A matches III.
Step 2: Match $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2$ (B). It dissociates into $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]^{2+} + 2\text{Cl}^-$. This produces $3$ ions ($1:2$ electrolyte) and precipitates $2\text{ mol}$ of $\text{AgCl}$: B matches IV.
Step 3: Match $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]\text{Cl}$ (C). It dissociates into $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]^+ + \text{Cl}^-$. This produces $2$ ions ($1:1$ electrolyte) and precipitates $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{AgCl}$: C matches I.
Step 4: Match $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_3\text{Cl}_3]$ (D). All chloride ions reside inside the coordination sphere. It is a neutral complex (non-electrolyte) and yields no precipitate of $\text{AgCl}$: D matches II. The matching sequence is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the structural distortion in copper(II) coordination entities:
Statement I: In the hexaaquacopper(II) complex $[\text{Cu}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$, the six copper-oxygen bonds are not equivalent, displaying two elongated axial bonds and four shorter equatorial bonds (tetragonal elongation).
Statement II: According to the Jahn-Teller theorem, any non-linear molecular system in a degenerate electronic ground state undergoes geometrical distortion that removes the electronic degeneracy and lowers the overall energy.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
B) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
D) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. The $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ ion has a $3d^9$ configuration, which in an octahedral field splits into $t_{2g}^6 e_g^3$. The three electrons in the $e_g$ orbitals are distributed asymmetrically: $(d_{z^2})^2 (d_{x^2-y^2})^1$. The two electrons in the $d_{z^2}$ orbital exert greater electrostatic repulsion along the $z$-axis, repelling the two axial water molecules further away. This results in two elongated axial bonds and four shorter equatorial bonds (tetragonally elongated octahedron). Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. The Jahn-Teller theorem states: 'Any non-linear molecular system in a spatially degenerate electronic state is unstable and will undergo distortion to lower its symmetry and remove the degeneracy.' In copper(II), the ground state $e_g^3$ is doubly degenerate; tetragonal distortion splits the $e_g$ orbitals into $d_{z^2}$ (lower energy) and $d_{x^2-y^2}$ (higher energy), thereby lowering the electronic energy. Statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The reaction of tetrachloridoplatinate(II) $[\text{PtCl}_4]^{2-}$ with two equivalents of ammonia selectively produces cisplatin, $cis\text{-}[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$, rather than the trans-isomer.
Reason (R): In square planar platinum(II) substitution reactions, the trans-directing ability of the coordinated chloride ligand ($\text{Cl}^-$) is stronger than that of the ammine ligand ($\text{NH}_3$).
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) (A) is false but (R) is true
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
C) (A) is true but (R) is false
D) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand the trans-effect in square planar complexes. The trans-effect is the ability of a coordinated ligand to direct an incoming nucleophilic substitution to the coordination position trans (opposite) to itself. The trans-directing series gives: $\text{Cl}^- > \text{NH}_3$.
Step 2: Analyze the synthesis of cisplatin from $[\text{PtCl}_4]^{2-}$. When the first $\text{NH}_3$ replaces a $\text{Cl}^-$, the mono-substituted intermediate $[\text{PtCl}_3(\text{NH}_3)]^-$ is formed. In this intermediate, the two chloride ligands trans to each other have a stronger trans-directing effect than the ammine ligand. Therefore, the incoming second $\text{NH}_3$ ligand selectively replaces a chloride ligand that is trans to another chloride, placing the two $\text{NH}_3$ ligands mutually cis to each other. This yields $cis\text{-}[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$ (cisplatin).
Step 3: Relate (A) and (R). Assertion (A) is true, Reason (R) is true, and (R) provides the exact theoretical and kinetic explanation for (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the spectrochemical series and molecular orbital interactions:
Statement I: Halide ions are positioned at the weak-field end of the spectrochemical series because their filled $p$-orbitals act as $\pi$-donors toward metal $d$-orbitals, which destabilizes the $t_{2g}$ orbitals and decreases $\Delta_o$.
Statement II: Ligands like $\text{CO}$ and $\text{CN}^-$ are positioned at the strong-field end of the spectrochemical series because they possess low-lying empty $\pi^*$ orbitals that act as $\pi$-acceptors, which stabilizes the $t_{2g}$ orbitals and dramatically increases $\Delta_o$.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
C) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
D) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. Halide ions ($	ext{I}^-, 	ext{Br}^-, 	ext{Cl}^-, 	ext{F}^-$) have filled valence $p$-orbitals perpendicular to the metal-ligand $\sigma$-axis. These filled orbitals overlap with the metal $t_{2g}$ orbitals in a $\pi$-donor fashion. The resulting antibonding $\pi^*$ molecular orbitals (predominantly metal $t_{2g}$ in character) are raised in energy closer to the $e_g^*$ level, significantly reducing the energy gap $\Delta_o$. Hence, $\pi$-donor ligands produce weak crystal fields. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. Ligands like $\text{CO}$ and $\text{CN}^-$ have vacant low-energy $\pi^*$ molecular orbitals. Overlap between the filled metal $t_{2g}$ orbitals and these empty ligand $\pi^*$ orbitals ($\pi$-backbonding) lowers the energy of the bonding $t_{2g}$ molecular orbitals. This increases the energy separation $\Delta_o$ between $t_{2g}$ and $e_g^*$. Hence, $\pi$-acceptor ligands produce very strong crystal fields. Statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Which of the following coordination entities exhibit optical isomerism (chirality)?
(1) $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_3]^{3+}$
(2) $cis\text{-}[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$
(3) $trans\text{-}[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$
(4) $[\text{Cr}(\text{ox})_3]^{3-}$
(5) $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$
Select the correct combination:
options: B) (1), (2), and (4) only
C) (2), (3), and (5) only
D) (1) and (4) only
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Examine (1) $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_3]^{3+}$. It is of the type $[\text{M}(\text{AA})_3]$. It adopts a propeller-like $D_3$ symmetry that lacks any plane of symmetry ($\sigma$) or center of inversion ($i$). It is chiral and exists as $\Delta$ (dextro) and $\Lambda$ (laevo) enantiomers. Hence, (1) exhibits optical isomerism.
Step 2: Examine (2) $cis\text{-}[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$. It is of type $cis\text{-}[\text{M}(\text{AA})_2\text{b}_2]$. It possesses only a $C_2$ axis and lacks an improper axis of rotation ($S_n$). It is chiral and exists as a pair of enantiomers. Hence, (2) exhibits optical isomerism.
Step 3: Examine (3) $trans\text{-}[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$. It possesses three mirror planes and an inversion center ($i$). It is achiral and optically inactive. It does not exhibit optical isomerism.
Step 4: Examine (4) $[\text{Cr}(\text{ox})_3]^{3-}$. Like $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_3]^{3+}$, it has three bidentate oxalate chelate rings in an octahedral arrangement ($D_3$ symmetry), making it chiral and optically active. Hence, (4) exhibits optical isomerism.
Step 5: Examine (5) $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$. This is a four-coordinate square planar complex. All square planar complexes have a horizontal plane of symmetry (the molecular plane itself) and are achiral. Hence, only (1), (2), and (4) exhibit optical isomerism.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Chelates containing five-membered rings formed by saturated bidentate ligands like ethane-1,2-diamine are generally more thermodynamically stable than those forming four-membered or seven-membered chelate rings.
Reason (R): Five-membered saturated chelate rings feature near-ideal tetrahedral bond angles ($109.5^\circ$) at carbon and nitrogen atoms with negligible Bayer angle strain, whereas four-membered rings suffer from severe bond angle strain and seven-membered rings experience unfavorable conformational entropy penalties.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) (A) is true but (R) is false
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
C) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
D) (A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). Chelate stability strongly depends on ring size. In general, for saturated chelating ligands without conjugated double bonds (such as ethylenediamine), five-membered rings form the most thermodynamically stable complexes (e.g., $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_3]^{3+}$). For conjugated ligands (like acetylacetonate), six-membered rings are also exceptionally stable. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). A four-membered chelate ring forces bond angles at the coordinating atoms to compress below $90^\circ$, producing severe ring strain. Seven-membered rings have greater conformational flexibility, incurring a substantial entropic penalty upon ring closure without compensatory enthalpy gain. In contrast, five-membered saturated rings achieve nearly staggered, strain-free conformations with minimal angle distortion. Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I (Octahedral Complex) with List II ($d$-electron configuration, CFSE, and spin-only magnetic moment $\mu_{\text{s}}$):

List I
A. $[\text{Mn}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$
B. $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$
C. $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$
D. $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$

List II
I. $t_{2g}^3 e_g^0$, $\text{CFSE} = -1.2\Delta_o$, $\mu_{\text{s}} \approx 3.87\text{ BM}$
II. $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$, $\text{CFSE} = -2.4\Delta_o + 2P$, $\mu_{\text{s}} = 0\text{ BM}$
III. $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$, $\text{CFSE} = 0.0\Delta_o$, $\mu_{\text{s}} \approx 5.92\text{ BM}$
IV. $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$, $\text{CFSE} = -0.4\Delta_o$, $\mu_{\text{s}} \approx 4.90\text{ BM}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III
B) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
C) A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
D) A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match $[\text{Mn}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ (A). $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ is $3d^5$. Water is a weak field ligand ($\Delta_o < P$), giving a high-spin configuration $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$. $\text{CFSE} = 3(-0.4) + 2(0.6) = 0.0\Delta_o$. With $5$ unpaired electrons, $\mu_{\text{s}} = \sqrt{5(7)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92\text{ BM}$: A matches III.
Step 2: Match $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ (B). $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ is $3d^3$. Configuration is $t_{2g}^3 e_g^0$. $\text{CFSE} = 3(-0.4) = -1.2\Delta_o$. With $3$ unpaired electrons, $\mu_{\text{s}} = \sqrt{3(5)} = \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87\text{ BM}$: B matches I.
Step 3: Match $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ (C). $\text{Co}^{3+}$ is $3d^6$. Ammonia is a strong field ligand for $\text{Co}^{3+}$, producing low-spin $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$. $\text{CFSE} = -2.4\Delta_o + 2P$. With $0$ unpaired electrons, $\mu_{\text{s}} = 0\text{ BM}$ (diamagnetic): C matches II.
Step 4: Match $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ (D). $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ is $3d^6$. Water is weak field, giving high-spin $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$. $\text{CFSE} = 4(-0.4) + 2(0.6) = -0.4\Delta_o$. With $4$ unpaired electrons, $\mu_{\text{s}} = \sqrt{4(6)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90\text{ BM}$: D matches IV. Hence, the match is A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding four-coordinate complexes of heavier transition elements:
Statement I: All four-coordinate complexes of divalent palladium ($\text{Pd}^{2+}$, $4d^8$) and divalent platinum ($\text{Pt}^{2+}$, $5d^8$) are square planar and diamagnetic, regardless of whether the coordinated ligands are halides or strong field ligands like cyanide.
Statement II: Moving down a triad from $3d$ to $4d$ and $5d$ transition metals, the crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta$) increases significantly (by approximately $30-50\%$), such that $\Delta$ exceeds the pairing energy ($P$) even with weak-field ligands.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. For $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ ($3d^8$), $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$ is tetrahedral and paramagnetic because $\text{Cl}^-$ cannot overcome pairing energy. However, for its heavier congeners $\text{Pd}^{2+}$ and $\text{Pt}^{2+}$, $[\text{PdCl}_4]^{2-}$ and $[\text{PtCl}_4]^{2-}$ are square planar ($dsp^2$) and diamagnetic. In fact, virtually all four-coordinate $\text{Pd(II)}$ and $\text{Pt(II)}$ complexes are square planar and diamagnetic. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. As principal quantum number increases from $3d$ to $4d$ to $5d$, the $d$-orbitals are more diffuse and extend further into space, interacting far more strongly with ligand orbitals. Consequently, the crystal field splitting $\Delta$ increases by roughly $40\%$ from $3d$ to $4d$ and another $25\%$ from $4d$ to $5d$. Concurrently, the larger orbital volume decreases inter-electronic repulsion, lowering the pairing energy $P$. Thus, $\Delta > P$ is universally satisfied for $4d$ and $5d$ metals, forcing electron pairing and favoring low-spin square planar geometry. Statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
A coordination compound $\text{X}$ having the empirical formula $\text{CrCl}_3 \cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$ undergoes the following reactions:
(i) An aqueous solution of $0.01\text{ mol}$ of $\text{X}$ requires exactly $20\text{ mL}$ of $1.0\text{ M } \text{AgNO}_3$ solution for complete precipitation of chloride ions.
(ii) Dehydration of $0.01\text{ mol}$ of solid $\text{X}$ over concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ results in a mass loss of $0.18\text{ g}$.
Based on these observations, which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding compound $\text{X}$?
options: A) The secondary valency of chromium in compound $\text{X}$ is $6$
B) Compound $\text{X}$ exhibits geometrical (cis-trans) isomerism
C) Its aqueous solution exhibits an electrical conductivity corresponding to a $1:2$ electrolyte
D) The IUPAC name of compound $\text{X}$ is pentaaquachloridochromium(III) chloride monohydrate
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Calculate the moles of ionisable chloride ions per mole of complex. Moles of $\text{Ag}^+$ consumed = $V \times M = 0.020\text{ L} \times 1.0\text{ mol/L} = 0.02\text{ mol}$. Since $0.01\text{ mol}$ of $\text{X}$ reacts with $0.02\text{ mol}$ of $\text{AgNO}_3$, there are $\frac{0.02}{0.01} = 2$ ionisable chloride ions per formula unit in the outer sphere ($\text{Cl}_2$).
Step 2: Calculate the moles of water of crystallization per mole of complex. Moles of water lost = $\frac{0.18\text{ g}}{18\text{ g/mol}} = 0.01\text{ mol}$. Since $0.01\text{ mol}$ of $\text{X}$ loses $0.01\text{ mol}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, there is exactly $1$ water molecule of crystallization outside the coordination sphere ($\cdot \text{H}_2\text{O}$).
Step 3: Deduce the coordination formula. The remaining five water molecules and one chloride ion are coordinated to $\text{Cr}^{3+}$: $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2 \cdot \text{H}_2\text{O}$.
Step 4: Evaluate each statement:
- Secondary valency is the coordination number: $5$ aqua $+ 1$ chlorido = $6$. (Correct)
- IUPAC name: pentaaquachloridochromium(III) chloride monohydrate. (Correct)
- Ionisation: $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5\text{Cl}]^{2+} + 2\text{Cl}^-$, which is a $1:2$ electrolyte. (Correct)
- Geometrical isomerism: The complex cation is of the type $[\text{Ma}_5\text{b}]$. Octahedral complexes of type $[\text{Ma}_5\text{b}]$ have only one spatial arrangement and CANNOT exhibit cis-trans geometrical isomerism. Therefore, statement D is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): An aqueous solution of the titanium(III) coordination complex $[\text{Ti}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ exhibits a distinctive purple/violet color.
Reason (R): The complex absorbs light in the blue-green region of visible radiation (wavelength $\approx 498\text{ nm}$) to promote a single $d$-electron from the $t_{2g}$ level to the $e_g$ level, and the transmitted light corresponds to the complementary purple/violet color.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) (A) is true but (R) is false
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
C) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
D) (A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). Titanium is element $22$; $\text{Ti}^{3+}$ has the valence configuration $[\text{Ar}]\,3d^1$. In $[\text{Ti}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$, the single $d$-electron resides in the lower $t_{2g}$ set: $t_{2g}^1 e_g^0$. Solutions of this complex are famously purple-violet in color. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). The crystal field splitting $\Delta_o$ for $[\text{Ti}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ is approximately $20,000\text{ cm}^{-1}$ ($240\text{ kJ/mol}$), which corresponds to the absorption of light at a wavelength of $\lambda = \frac{hc}{\Delta_o} \approx 498\text{ nm}$ (in the blue-green region). When white light passes through the solution, the blue-green light is absorbed to excite the electron from $t_{2g}$ to $e_g$. The transmitted light, being deficient in blue-green, appears purple-violet (its complementary color). Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding a Daniell cell operating under standard conditions:
Statement I: A salt bridge contains an agar-agar gel mixed with an inert electrolyte such as $\text{KCl}$, $\text{KNO}_3$, or $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$, whose ionic mobilities of cation and anion are nearly equal.
Statement II: The primary functions of the salt bridge are to complete the electrical circuit by allowing the flow of ions and to prevent liquid junction potential by maintaining electrical neutrality in both half-cells.
Choose the correct option:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. In a galvanic cell like the Daniell cell, the salt bridge is an inverted U-tube packed with agar-agar gel or gelatin containing an inert electrolyte like $\text{KCl}$, $\text{KNO}_3$, or $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$. The velocities (transference numbers/mobilities) of the cation and anion must be nearly identical so that no electrical imbalance develops at the junctions. Hence, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. The salt bridge allows ions to migrate between half-cells to neutralize accumulating charges (excess $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ in the anodic compartment and excess $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ in the cathodic compartment), thereby maintaining electrical neutrality and eliminating the liquid junction potential while completing the internal circuit without bulk mixing of solutions. Hence, Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The standard electrode potential of the Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE) is arbitrarily assigned a value of $0.00\text{ V}$ at all temperatures.
Reason (R): The potential of an isolated single half-cell cannot be measured directly because neither oxidation nor reduction can occur in isolation.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) (A) is false but (R) is true.
B) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
C) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
D) (A) is true but (R) is false.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand the measurement of half-cell potential. An individual half-cell reaction (oxidation or reduction) involves electron transfer that cannot take place without a complementary half-cell to supply or accept electrons. Therefore, absolute electrode potential cannot be measured experimentally. Reason (R) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate standard reference. Because individual potentials cannot be determined independently, IUPAC assigned the Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE), represented as $\text{Pt}(s)|\text{H}_2(g, 1\text{ bar})|\text{H}^+(aq, 1\text{ M})$, a reference potential of exactly $0.00\text{ V}$ at all temperatures. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 3: Relate (A) and (R). Because single electrode potentials cannot be measured in isolation, an arbitrary standard reference (SHE = $0.00\text{ V}$) is necessitated to measure relative potentials of other electrodes. Hence, Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Conclusion: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding the conventions and components of a standard galvanic cell $\text{Zn}(s)|\text{Zn}^{2+}(aq)\|\text{Cu}^{2+}(aq)|\text{Cu}(s)$:
List I:
(P) Anode electrode
(Q) Cathode electrode
(R) Direction of electron flow in external circuit
(S) Direction of conventional electric current
List II:
(1) From copper electrode to zinc electrode
(2) Oxidation site where zinc dissolves as $\text{Zn}^{2+}$
(3) From zinc electrode to copper electrode
(4) Reduction site where $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ deposits as copper
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify Anode (P). In a Daniell cell, oxidation occurs at the zinc plate (anode): $\text{Zn}(s) \to \text{Zn}^{2+}(aq) + 2e^-$, so zinc dissolves. Thus, P matches (2).
Step 2: Identify Cathode (Q). Reduction occurs at the copper plate (cathode): $\text{Cu}^{2+}(aq) + 2e^- \to \text{Cu}(s)$, so copper deposits. Thus, Q matches (4).
Step 3: Identify Electron Flow (R). Electrons are released at the anode (zinc) and migrate through the external metallic wire to the cathode (copper). Thus, R matches (3).
Step 4: Identify Conventional Current (S). Conventional electric current flows in the direction opposite to electron flow, i.e., from cathode (copper) to anode (zinc). Thus, S matches (1).
Conclusion: The correct matching sequence is P-2, Q-4, R-3, S-1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: An external opposing potential ($E_{\text{ext}}$) is applied across a Daniell cell having a standard electromotive force of $1.10\text{ V}$. Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: A) When $E_{\text{ext}} < 1.10\text{ V}$, electrons flow from the zinc rod to the copper rod and current flows from copper to zinc.
B) When $E_{\text{ext}} = 1.10\text{ V}$, no chemical reaction takes place and current ceases to flow.
C) When $E_{\text{ext}} > 1.10\text{ V}$, the cell functions as an electrolytic cell with electrons flowing from copper to zinc.
D) When $E_{\text{ext}} > 1.10\text{ V}$, zinc dissolves at the zinc electrode and copper deposits on the copper electrode.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Daniell cell behavior when $E_{\text{ext}} < 1.10\text{ V}$. The cell operates spontaneously as a galvanic cell: zinc dissolves at the anode, copper deposits at the cathode, electrons flow from $\text{Zn}$ to $\text{Cu}$, and current flows from $\text{Cu}$ to $\text{Zn}$.
Step 2: Analyze Daniell cell behavior when $E_{\text{ext}} = 1.10\text{ V}$. The opposing EMF exactly balances the cell potential. No net electron flow occurs, no current passes, and no chemical reaction takes place.
Step 3: Analyze Daniell cell behavior when $E_{\text{ext}} > 1.10\text{ V}$. The external source overcomes the cell EMF, reversing the direction of current. The cell now acts as an electrolytic cell: electrons flow from $\text{Cu}$ to $\text{Zn}$, copper dissolves at the copper electrode ($	ext{Cu} \to \text{Cu}^{2+} + 2e^-$), and zinc deposits at the zinc electrode ($	ext{Zn}^{2+} + 2e^- \to \text{Zn}$). Statement D claims zinc dissolves and copper deposits, which is the galvanic mode, making Statement D incorrect.
Conclusion: The incorrect statement is that when $E_{\text{ext}} > 1.10\text{ V}$, zinc dissolves at the zinc electrode and copper deposits on the copper electrode.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding standard reduction potentials ($E^\circ$) at $298\text{ K}$:
Statement I: A species with a more positive standard reduction potential has a higher tendency to get reduced and acts as a stronger oxidizing agent.
Statement II: Fluorine gas ($\text{F}_2$) has the highest positive standard reduction potential ($+2.87\text{ V}$) in the electrochemical series, making it the strongest oxidizing agent, while lithium ion ($\text{Li}^+$) has the most negative potential ($-3.05\text{ V}$), making lithium metal the strongest reducing agent in aqueous solution.
Choose the correct option:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. By IUPAC convention, standard electrode potentials are expressed as reduction potentials. A greater positive value of $E^\circ$ indicates a stronger thermodynamic tendency to gain electrons (undergo reduction). A substance that readily reduces itself acts as a strong oxidizing agent. Hence, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. According to NCERT electrochemical series data at $298\text{ K}$, $\text{F}_2(g) + 2e^- \to 2\text{F}^-$ has $E^\circ = +2.87\text{ V}$ (highest positive value, making $\text{F}_2$ the most powerful oxidizing agent). Conversely, $\text{Li}^+ + e^- \to \text{Li}(s)$ has $E^\circ = -3.05\text{ V}$ (most negative value, meaning $\text{Li}$ oxidizes extremely readily, making metallic $\text{Li}$ the strongest reducing agent in aqueous medium). Hence, Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I (Physical Quantity) with List II (SI / Conventional Unit and Formula):
List I:
(P) Conductivity ($\kappa$)
(Q) Cell constant ($G^*$)
(R) Molar conductivity ($\Lambda_m$)
(S) Conductance ($G$)
List II:
(1) $\text{S m}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$ or $\text{S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$
(2) $\text{S}$ (Siemens) or $\Omega^{-1}$
(3) $\text{S m}^{-1}$ or $\text{S cm}^{-1}$
(4) $\text{m}^{-1}$ or $\text{cm}^{-1}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Determine unit of Conductivity ($\kappa$). Conductivity is the inverse of resistivity: $\kappa = \frac{1}{\rho} = \frac{l}{R \cdot A}$. Its SI unit is $\text{S m}^{-1}$, and commonly $\text{S cm}^{-1}$. Thus, P matches (3).
Step 2: Determine unit of Cell constant ($G^*$). $G^* = \frac{l}{A}$. Length divided by area gives dimension of $\text{length}^{-1}$, with units $\text{m}^{-1}$ or $\text{cm}^{-1}$. Thus, Q matches (4).
Step 3: Determine unit of Molar conductivity ($\Lambda_m$). $\Lambda_m = \frac{\kappa}{c}$, with units $\frac{\text{S m}^{-1}}{\text{mol m}^{-3}} = \text{S m}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$ or $\text{S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$. Thus, R matches (1).
Step 4: Determine unit of Conductance ($G$). Conductance is the reciprocal of resistance: $G = \frac{1}{R}$, measured in Siemens ($\text{S}$) or $\Omega^{-1}$. Thus, S matches (2).
Conclusion: The correct matching is P-3, Q-4, R-1, S-2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): In measuring the electrical resistance of an electrolytic solution using a Wheatstone bridge, an alternating current (AC) source in the audio frequency range is used instead of a direct current (DC) source.
Reason (R): Passing direct current through an electrolytic solution causes electrolysis, which alters the chemical composition and concentration of the solution near the electrodes.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) (A) is false but (R) is true.
B) (A) is true but (R) is false.
C) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
D) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). To measure the resistance of an electrolytic solution using a Wheatstone bridge, a standard direct current cannot be employed; instead, an alternating current (AC) source typically operating in the frequency range of $550$ to $5000\text{ Hz}$ is employed. Thus, Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). If direct current (DC) were passed through the solution, continuous electrolysis would take place, liberating gases or depositing metals at the electrodes. This leads to polarization of electrodes and alters the chemical composition of the electrolyte in the cell. Thus, Reason (R) is true.
Step 3: Relate (A) and (R). The AC source reverses the current polarity thousands of times per second, preventing net electrolysis and polarization. Hence, Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A).
Conclusion: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding the variation of conductivity ($\kappa$) of an electrolytic solution upon dilution:
Statement I: Conductivity ($\kappa$) is defined as the conductance of a solution enclosed between two electrodes of unit cross-sectional area separated by unit length, which corresponds to the conductance of one unit volume ($1\text{ cm}^3$ or $1\text{ m}^3$) of the solution.
Statement II: On increasing dilution, conductivity ($\kappa$) increases for strong electrolytes but decreases for weak electrolytes.
Choose the correct option:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. By definition, $G = \kappa \frac{A}{l}$. When $A = 1\text{ cm}^2$ and $l = 1\text{ cm}$, conductance $G = \kappa$. This represents the electrical conductance of a $1\text{ cm}^3$ unit volume of the electrolytic solution. Hence, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. Conductivity always decreases with decrease in concentration (i.e., upon dilution) for both strong and weak electrolytes. This is because dilution decreases the total number of current-carrying ions per unit volume ($1\text{ mL}$ or $1\text{ cm}^3$) of the solution. Hence, Statement II is incorrect.
Conclusion: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding molar conductivity ($\Lambda_m$) of electrolytes:
Statement I: Molar conductivity of a solution at a given concentration is the conductance of volume $V$ of solution containing one mole of electrolyte kept between two electrodes with area of cross-section $A$ and distance of unit length.
Statement II: Molar conductivity increases with decrease in concentration because the increase in volume $V$ containing one mole of electrolyte on dilution more than compensates for the decrease in conductivity ($\kappa$).
Choose the correct option:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. According to NCERT, molar conductivity $\Lambda_m = \kappa V$, where $V$ is the volume of the solution containing exactly one mole of electrolyte placed between two sufficiently large electrodes unit distance apart. Hence, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. On dilution, although conductivity $\kappa$ (conductance per unit volume) decreases, the total volume $V$ containing one mole of electrolyte increases substantially ($V = 1/c$). The product $\kappa \times V$ increases because the proportional expansion in volume exceeds the proportional decrease in conductivity. Therefore, $\Lambda_m$ always increases with dilution for both strong and weak electrolytes. Hence, Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The limiting molar conductivities ($\Lambda_m^\circ$) at $298\text{ K}$ for $\text{NaCl}$, $\text{KBr}$, and $\text{KCl}$ are $126.4$, $151.8$, and $149.8\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$, respectively. Using Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions, calculate the limiting molar conductivity of $\text{NaBr}$ at $298\text{ K}$:
options: A) $175.2\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$
B) $128.4\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$
C) $124.4\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$
D) $147.8\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Formulate the relationship using Kohlrausch's law.
According to Kohlrausch's law:
$\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{NaBr}) = \lambda^\circ(\text{Na}^+) + \lambda^\circ(\text{Br}^-)$
Step 2: Express $\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{NaBr})$ in terms of the given salts:
$\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{NaBr}) = \Lambda_m^\circ(\text{NaCl}) + \Lambda_m^\circ(\text{KBr}) - \Lambda_m^\circ(\text{KCl})$
Step 3: Substitute the numerical values:
$\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{NaBr}) = 126.4 + 151.8 - 149.8$
$\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{NaBr}) = 278.2 - 149.8 = 128.4\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$
Conclusion: The limiting molar conductivity of $\text{NaBr}$ is $128.4\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A steady electric current of $1.50\text{ A}$ is passed through an aqueous solution of silver nitrate ($\text{AgNO}_3$) for exactly $16\text{ minutes}$ and $5\text{ seconds}$. What is the mass of silver deposited at the cathode? (Molar mass of $\text{Ag} = 108\text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $1\text{ F} = 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1}$)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Calculate the total time in seconds.
$t = (16 \times 60) + 5 = 960 + 5 = 965\text{ s}$.
Step 2: Calculate the total charge passed ($Q$).
$Q = I \times t = 1.50\text{ A} \times 965\text{ s} = 1447.5\text{ C}$.
Step 3: Determine the reduction reaction and number of electrons transferred.
$\text{Ag}^+ + e^- \to \text{Ag}(s)$
Thus, $1\text{ mol}$ of electrons ($96500\text{ C}$) deposits $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Ag}$ ($108\text{ g}$).
Step 4: Calculate the deposited mass ($w$).
$w = \frac{Q \times M}{n \times F} = \frac{1447.5 \times 108}{1 \times 96500} = \frac{1.5 \times 965 \times 108}{96500} = \frac{1.5 \times 108}{100} = \frac{162}{100} = 1.62\text{ g}$.
Conclusion: The mass of silver deposited at the cathode is $1.62\text{ g}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding Faraday's laws of electrolysis:
Statement I: Faraday's first law states that the mass of a substance deposited or liberated at any electrode during electrolysis is directly proportional to the quantity of electricity passed through the electrolyte.
Statement II: Faraday's second law states that when the same quantity of electricity is passed through solutions of different electrolytes connected in parallel, the masses of substances liberated are directly proportional to their equivalent weights.
Choose the correct option:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. According to Faraday's first law, $m \propto Q$, or $m = zIt$, where $m$ is the mass deposited or liberated, $Q$ is the electric charge passed, and $z$ is the electrochemical equivalent. Hence, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. Faraday's second law explicitly states that the same quantity of electricity must pass through the cells, which requires the electrolytic cells to be connected in SERIES, not in parallel. In a parallel circuit, current divides among branches based on resistance, so different quantities of electricity would pass through different cells. Hence, Statement II is incorrect.
Conclusion: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): During the electrolysis of concentrated aqueous sodium chloride solution (brine) using inert platinum electrodes, chlorine gas ($\text{Cl}_2$) is liberated at the anode rather than oxygen gas ($\text{O}_2$).
Reason (R): Although the oxidation of water to produce oxygen has a lower standard reduction potential than the oxidation of chloride ions, oxygen evolution is kinetically slow and requires an extra potential known as overpotential.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
C) (A) is true but (R) is false.
D) (A) is false but (R) is true.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate the anodic reactions in brine electrolysis.
Possible oxidation reactions at the anode:
$2\text{Cl}^-(aq) \to \text{Cl}_2(g) + 2e^-$, $E^\circ_{\text{ox}} = -1.36\text{ V}$
$2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \to \text{O}_2(g) + 4\text{H}^+(aq) + 4e^-$, $E^\circ_{\text{ox}} = -1.23\text{ V}$
Thermodynamically, oxidation of water has a lower potential ($1.23\text{ V} < 1.36\text{ V}$) and should be preferred.
Step 2: Evaluate the kinetic effect (overpotential). The oxidation of water involves a complex four-electron transfer producing oxygen, which has very slow reaction kinetics on platinum. It demands significant extra energy termed 'overpotential' (overvoltage). Because of this overpotential of oxygen, the oxidation of chloride ions to $\text{Cl}_2$ becomes kinetically preferred. Thus, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are both true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Conclusion: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the electrolysis of an aqueous copper(II) sulfate ($\text{CuSO}_4$) solution under two different conditions:
Condition 1: Electrolysis using inert platinum electrodes.
Condition 2: Electrolysis using attackable copper electrodes.
Which of the following statements correctly describes the anodic processes?
options: A) In Condition 1, copper dissolves at the anode, while in Condition 2, oxygen gas is evolved at the anode.
B) In Condition 1, oxygen gas is evolved at the anode, while in Condition 2, copper dissolves from the anode into the solution as $\text{Cu}^{2+}$.
C) In both Condition 1 and Condition 2, oxygen gas is evolved at the anode.
D) In both Condition 1 and Condition 2, copper metal deposits on the anode.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Condition 1 (inert platinum electrodes). Platinum does not take part in the chemical reaction. At the cathode, copper is deposited: $\text{Cu}^{2+} + 2e^- \to \text{Cu}$. At the anode, water is oxidized in preference to sulfate ions: $2\text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{O}_2 + 4\text{H}^+ + 4e^-$, liberating oxygen gas and generating sulfuric acid.
Step 2: Analyze Condition 2 (copper electrodes). Since copper is an active/attackable electrode, the oxidation potential of metallic copper ($E^\circ_{\text{Cu}/\text{Cu}^{2+}} = -0.34\text{ V}$) is far higher than that of water ($-1.23\text{ V}$) or sulfate. Consequently, the copper anode itself undergoes oxidation: $\text{Cu}(s) \to \text{Cu}^{2+}(aq) + 2e^-$, dissolving into solution.
Conclusion: In Condition 1, oxygen gas is evolved at the anode, while in Condition 2, copper dissolves from the anode into the solution as $\text{Cu}^{2+}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding the Leclanché dry cell:
Statement I: In a commercial dry cell, the zinc cylinder acts as the anode, and a carbon (graphite) rod surrounded by powdered manganese dioxide ($\text{MnO}_2$) and carbon acts as the cathode.
Statement II: During discharge, manganese is reduced from the $+4$ oxidation state in $\text{MnO}_2$ to the $+3$ oxidation state in $\text{MnO(OH)}$, and the ammonia released at the cathode combines with $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ to form the complex $[\text{Zn}(\text{NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$.
Choose the correct option:
options: A) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
D) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. In the standard Leclanché dry cell, the outer zinc container serves as the anode, and a graphite rod placed centrally and surrounded by powdered $\text{MnO}_2$ and carbon black serves as the cathode. The space between is filled with a moist paste of $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ and $\text{ZnCl}_2$. Hence, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. The half-reactions are:
Anode: $\text{Zn}(s) \to \text{Zn}^{2+} + 2e^-$
Cathode: $\text{MnO}_2 + \text{NH}_4^+ + e^- \to \text{MnO(OH)} + \text{NH}_3$
In $\text{MnO}_2$, Mn is in $+4$ oxidation state; in $\text{MnO(OH)}$, Mn is in $+3$ state. Free $\text{NH}_3$ gas could build up internal pressure, but it coordinates with $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ ions from the electrolyte to yield $[\text{Zn}(\text{NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$, preventing gas build-up. Hence, Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The cell potential of a miniature mercury cell remains remarkably constant at approximately $1.35\text{ V}$ throughout its operational life.
Reason (R): The overall chemical reaction of the mercury cell does not involve any ions in the electrolytic solution whose concentrations could change during operation.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
B) (A) is true but (R) is false.
C) (A) is false but (R) is true.
D) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). A mercury cell, used in hearing aids and watches, produces a steady voltage of about $1.35\text{ V}$ that remains practically unvarying until exhaustion. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). The electrode reactions in a mercury cell are:
Anode: $\text{Zn(Hg)} + 2\text{OH}^- \to \text{ZnO}(s) + \text{H}_2\text{O} + 2e^-$
Cathode: $\text{HgO}(s) + \text{H}_2\text{O} + 2e^- \to \text{Hg}(l) + 2\text{OH}^-$
Overall reaction: $\text{Zn(Hg)} + \text{HgO}(s) \to \text{ZnO}(s) + \text{Hg}(l)$
The overall reaction contains only solid and liquid phases (amalgam, $\text{ZnO}$, $\text{HgO}$, $\text{Hg}$), with no ionic species in solution whose concentration changes during discharge. Reason (R) is true.
Step 3: Relate (A) and (R). According to the Nernst equation, cell potential depends on ion concentrations ($E = E^\circ - \frac{RT}{nF}\ln Q$). Because $Q$ is constant, $E$ remains invariant throughout cell life. Hence, Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Conclusion: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I (Electrode / Component in Lead Storage Battery) with List II (Composition / Chemical Role during Discharge):
List I:
(P) Anode grid
(Q) Cathode grid
(R) Electrolyte
(S) Insoluble precipitate formed at both electrodes
List II:
(1) Lead dioxide ($\text{PbO}_2$)
(2) Lead sulfate ($\text{PbSO}_4$)
(3) Spongy lead ($\text{Pb}$)
(4) $38\%$ by mass sulfuric acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, density $\sim 1.30\text{ g mL}^{-1}$)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify Anode (P). In a lead storage battery, the anode consists of a lead grid packed with finely divided spongy lead. Thus, P matches (3).
Step 2: Identify Cathode (Q). The cathode is a lead grid packed with lead dioxide ($\text{PbO}_2$). Thus, Q matches (1).
Step 3: Identify Electrolyte (R). The electrolyte is an aqueous solution of sulfuric acid, approximately $38\%$ by mass with a density of $1.30\text{ g mL}^{-1}$. Thus, R matches (4).
Step 4: Identify Precipitate (S). During discharge, lead is oxidized at the anode to form insoluble $\text{PbSO}_4(s)$, and $\text{PbO}_2$ is reduced at the cathode to also form insoluble $\text{PbSO}_4(s)$. Thus, S matches (2).
Conclusion: The correct matching is P-3, Q-1, R-4, S-2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding the recharging process of a secondary lead storage battery:
Statement I: During recharging, the battery is connected to an external DC power source such that the negative terminal is connected to the lead electrode and the positive terminal is connected to the $\text{PbO}_2$ electrode.
Statement II: During the recharge process, $\text{PbSO}_4(s)$ on the anode is reduced back to spongy $\text{Pb}(s)$, $\text{PbSO}_4(s)$ on the cathode is oxidized back to $\text{PbO}_2(s)$, and sulfuric acid is regenerated, increasing the electrolyte density.
Choose the correct option:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. During recharge, the lead storage battery operates as an electrolytic cell. The polarity must oppose discharge: the negative terminal of the external source is connected to the spongy lead electrode (where reduction must occur), and the positive terminal is connected to the $\text{PbO}_2$ electrode (where oxidation must occur). Hence, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. The reverse reactions during recharging are:
At negative electrode (cathode during electrolysis): $\text{PbSO}_4(s) + 2e^- \to \text{Pb}(s) + \text{SO}_4^{2-}(aq)$
At positive electrode (anode during electrolysis): $\text{PbSO}_4(s) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{PbO}_2(s) + \text{SO}_4^{2-}(aq) + 4\text{H}^+(aq) + 2e^-$
Overall recharge reaction: $2\text{PbSO}_4(s) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \to \text{Pb}(s) + \text{PbO}_2(s) + 2\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4(aq)$.
Sulfuric acid is regenerated, which restores the density of the acid solution. Hence, Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The Nickel-Cadmium (Ni-Cd) cell is a rechargeable secondary cell that possesses a longer operational lifespan than the conventional lead storage battery.
Reason (R): The overall chemical reaction occurring during the discharge of a Ni-Cd cell is represented as:
$\text{Cd}(s) + 2\text{Ni(OH)}_3(s) \to \text{CdO}(s) + 2\text{Ni(OH)}_2(s) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) (A) is false but (R) is true.
B) (A) is true but (R) is false.
C) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
D) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). According to NCERT, the nickel-cadmium cell is another important rechargeable secondary cell. It has a significantly longer lifespan and higher reliability than a lead storage battery, though it is more expensive to manufacture. Thus, Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). During discharge, cadmium metal at the anode is oxidized, and nickel(III) hydroxide at the cathode is reduced to nickel(II) hydroxide. The overall reaction given in NCERT is: $\text{Cd}(s) + 2\text{Ni(OH)}_3(s) \to \text{CdO}(s) + 2\text{Ni(OH)}_2(s) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$. Thus, Reason (R) is true.
Step 3: Relate (A) and (R). While Reason (R) correctly specifies the stoichiometric discharge reaction, the extended longevity of the cell arises from the mechanical stability and reversibility of the insoluble hydroxide phases adhering to the electrode grids without corrosive acid degradation. Therefore, Reason (R) is a true statement but not the causal explanation of (A).
Conclusion: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements regarding the hydrogen-oxygen ($\text{H}_2\text{-O}_2$) fuel cell is INCORRECT?
options: A) Porous carbon electrodes impregnated with finely divided catalysts like platinum or palladium are used.
B) The electrolyte is a concentrated aqueous solution of sodium hydroxide or potassium hydroxide.
C) The thermodynamic electrical efficiency of a fuel cell is approximately $70\%$, compared to about $40\%$ for conventional thermal power plants.
D) During cell operation, oxygen is bubbled through the anode compartment and hydrogen is bubbled through the cathode compartment.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze electrode gas feeds. In an alkaline $\text{H}_2\text{-O}_2$ fuel cell, hydrogen gas is fed into the anode compartment where it undergoes oxidation: $2\text{H}_2(g) + 4\text{OH}^-(aq) \to 4\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) + 4e^-$. Oxygen gas is fed into the cathode compartment where it undergoes reduction: $\text{O}_2(g) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) + 4e^- \to 4\text{OH}^-(aq)$. Statement D reverses these feeds (claims oxygen at anode and hydrogen at cathode), making Statement D incorrect.
Step 2: Check other statements against NCERT. Statement A is correct (porous carbon electrodes with Pt/Pd catalyst). Statement B is correct (concentrated aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ or $\text{KOH}$). Statement C is correct (efficiency $\sim 70\%$ vs $40\%$ in thermal plants).
Conclusion: The incorrect statement is that oxygen is bubbled through the anode compartment and hydrogen is bubbled through the cathode compartment.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding the electrochemical mechanism of corrosion (rusting) of iron:
Statement I: A particular spot on the surface of iron behaves as an anode where iron is oxidized to ferrous ions: $2\text{Fe}(s) \to 2\text{Fe}^{2+} + 4e^-$, with $E^\circ_{(\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe})} = -0.44\text{ V}$.
Statement II: The electrons released at the anodic spot move through the metal to another spot where they reduce atmospheric oxygen in the presence of $\text{H}^+$ ions: $\text{O}_2(g) + 4\text{H}^+(aq) + 4e^- \to 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$, with $E^\circ = +1.23\text{ V}$.
Choose the correct option:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. According to the electrochemical theory of rusting presented in NCERT, an anodic spot on the iron surface undergoes oxidation: $2\text{Fe}(s) \to 2\text{Fe}^{2+} + 4e^-$, where $E^\circ_{(\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe})} = -0.44\text{ V}$. Hence, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. The liberated electrons migrate through the iron metal to another surface area which acts as a cathode. In the presence of $\text{H}^+$ ions (derived from carbonic acid $\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$ formed by dissolution of atmospheric $\text{CO}_2$ in moisture), dissolved oxygen is reduced to water: $\text{O}_2(g) + 4\text{H}^+(aq) + 4e^- \to 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$, with $E^\circ = +1.23\text{ V}$. The overall cell potential is $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 1.23 - (-0.44) = +1.67\text{ V}$. Hence, Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Galvanized iron pipes coated with a layer of zinc do not rust even if the surface zinc coating is scratched or chipped.
Reason (R): Zinc has a more negative standard reduction potential ($E^\circ_{\text{Zn}^{2+}/\text{Zn}} = -0.76\text{ V}$) than iron ($E^\circ_{\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe}} = -0.44\text{ V}$), causing zinc to undergo sacrificial oxidation in preference to iron.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) (A) is false but (R) is true.
B) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
C) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
D) (A) is true but (R) is false.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). Galvanization is the coating of iron with metallic zinc. When the zinc layer is cracked or scratched, exposing the underlying iron, the iron still does not rust. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). Comparing the standard reduction potentials: $E^\circ_{\text{Zn}^{2+}/\text{Zn}} = -0.76\text{ V}$ and $E^\circ_{\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe}} = -0.44\text{ V}$. Because zinc has a more negative reduction potential, it has a greater oxidation tendency (more electropositive). Zinc acts as the anode and preferentially oxidizes ($\text{Zn} \to \text{Zn}^{2+} + 2e^-$), while iron acts as the cathode and remains protected. Reason (R) is true.
Step 3: Relate (A) and (R). Because zinc sacrifices itself by preferential oxidation due to its lower reduction potential, galvanized iron remains protected even when scratched. Hence, Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Conclusion: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the standard reduction potentials at $298\text{ K}$:
$E^\circ_{(\text{Cr}^{3+}/\text{Cr})} = -0.74\text{ V}$ and $E^\circ_{(\text{Cd}^{2+}/\text{Cd})} = -0.40\text{ V}$
For the spontaneous redox reaction:
$2\text{Cr}(s) + 3\text{Cd}^{2+}(aq) \to 2\text{Cr}^{3+}(aq) + 3\text{Cd}(s)$
Calculate the standard cell potential ($E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$) and standard Gibbs energy change ($\Delta_r G^\circ$). (Take $1\text{ F} = 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1}$)
options: A) $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = +0.34\text{ V}$, $\Delta_r G^\circ = -196.86\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
B) $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = +1.14\text{ V}$, $\Delta_r G^\circ = -660.06\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
C) $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = -0.34\text{ V}$, $\Delta_r G^\circ = +196.86\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
D) $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = +0.34\text{ V}$, $\Delta_r G^\circ = -98.43\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Determine the cathode and anode half-reactions.
Oxidation at Anode: $2\text{Cr}(s) \to 2\text{Cr}^{3+}(aq) + 6e^-$
Reduction at Cathode: $3\text{Cd}^{2+}(aq) + 6e^- \to 3\text{Cd}(s)$
The number of electrons transferred is $n = 6$.
Step 2: Calculate $E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$.
$E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cathode}} - E^\circ_{\text{anode}} = E^\circ_{(\text{Cd}^{2+}/\text{Cd})} - E^\circ_{(\text{Cr}^{3+}/\text{Cr})}$
$E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = -0.40\text{ V} - (-0.74\text{ V}) = +0.34\text{ V}$.
Step 3: Calculate $\Delta_r G^\circ$.
$\Delta_r G^\circ = -nFE^\circ_{\text{cell}} = -6 \times 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1} \times 0.34\text{ V}$
$\Delta_r G^\circ = -196860\text{ J mol}^{-1} = -196.86\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
Conclusion: $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = +0.34\text{ V}$ and $\Delta_r G^\circ = -196.86\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The reduction potential of a hydrogen electrode dipped in an aqueous solution of $\text{pH} = 10$ at $298\text{ K}$ with hydrogen gas maintained at $1\text{ bar}$ pressure is $-0.591\text{ V}$.
